learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems in materials science, technology, and chemistry using established methods.
Be able to design in Engineering under specific requirements.
Be able to design and conduct experiments to solve problems in materials science, technology, and chemistry, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Possess technical and laboratory competencies in materials science, technology, and chemistry.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve problems in materials science, technology, and chemistry.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems in materials science, technology, and chemistry.
Understand applicable methods and techniques in materials science, technology, and chemistry and their limitations.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering
Framework of Materials Science and Engineering. Concept
Relationship between structure, properties and processing
Nature and types of bonding in materials
Metallic bond. Band theory and other theories
Atomic positions, crystallographic directions and planes
Comparison between FCC, HCP and BCC crystal structures
Atomic density in crystals: linear, planar and volumetric
Perfect and imperfect crystals: thermodynamic considerations
Classification and dimension of defects: point, linear and surface
Defects: point, linear, planar and surface
Solid solutions in metals and ceramics
General concepts. Constituents, phases and components
Phase diagrams of single-component and binary systems
Classification of materials based on their electrical properties
Conductive Materials. Factors: temperature, existence of defects, impurities, etc.
Characterization methods and types of mechanical tests
Uniaxial tensile test: nominal stress and strain. True stress and strain
Classification. Ferrous and non-ferrous alloys. General characteristics of:
Obtaining metallic materials: Solidification: Nucleation and Growth
Forming by plastic deformation. Strain hardening
Steels: Equilibrium transformations in the Fe-C system
Steels: Non-equilibrium transformations in the Fe-C system
Bonding and general properties of ceramic materials
Thermal behavior: Thermal transitions: Tm and Tg
Classifications of polymers: Thermoplastics, thermosets and elastomers
Obtaining and applications of polymeric materials
Classification: type of reinforcement and matrix
Elastic properties (PMC with polymeric matrix and continuous fibers)
assessment_rules: It is compulsory to complete the laboratory practices to pass the course. Entry to the laboratory requires watching general and materials/chemistry lab safety videos and correctly answering both tests. Failure to attend the laboratory without justified cause implies failing the continuous assessment. A minimum score of 4.0 in the ordinary call exam is required to pass the course.
